$description: The Plenix design of each native component: what the Plenix guidance becomes as a real control. Per iOS page: the Apple kit default beside the same kit component styled with the Plenix variables (Figma), its anatomy, each attribute from the Plenix token to SwiftUI, UIKit and AppKit, its states and code. Images are renders of the Plenix Figma file; build-native-guidance.js checks every key, image and token.

android-actions|Button.summary: A Plenix button on Android is the Material 3 Button, kept native in behavior (the ripple, the 48 dp touch target, TalkBack’s button role, keyboard and D-pad focus, font scale) and styled with the Plenix tokens: a 6 dp rounded rectangle 40 dp tall, a DM Sans semibold label at the label text role (Label large) and the Plenix action colors. android-actions|Menu.summary: A Plenix menu on Android is the Material 3 menu (DropdownMenu in Compose, a popup list in Views), kept native in behavior (it opens from its button, closes on a tap outside or Back, moves focus with the keyboard or D-pad, and TalkBack reads its items) and styled with the Plenix menu tokens: an overlay surface with an 8 dp radius and a 1 dp border, 48 dp rows, DM Sans labels at the body text role and the Plenix danger and disabled colors. android-content|Avatar.summary: A Plenix avatar on Android is a small composable (a ShapeableImageView or a TextView in Views), since Material 3 has no avatar component: a person’s picture or initials in a rounded square, never a circle, with the corner and the text size following the size. Initials are DM Sans bold in the avatar colors; a person’s own color uses its soft fill and text color; a category uses its category color. It is hidden from TalkBack unless it carries a label. Material’s lists show a 40 dp circle; Plenix keeps the list placement and replaces the shape and colors.

android-data-display|Tree.summary: Plenix on Android shows a library’s folders the way the web’s file browser does: a tree of folders in a list, each row an expand control, the folder icon and its name in DM Sans, the open folder in the selected fill, and its contents beside it on a large screen (a list-detail layout) or as the next screen on a phone, where the path above the list leads back. Material 3 has no tree component; Plenix builds it from list items with Material’s expand and collapse, its touch targets and TalkBack’s expanded state, and changes the look: Plenix colors, DM Sans and DM Mono, the Plenix row height and the line between rows. Files move by dragging them onto a folder (a long press) or with Move to in the row’s menu.

android-forms|Slider.summary: A Plenix slider on Android is the Material 3 Slider, kept native in behavior (dragging or tapping the track, steps that snap, TalkBack reading the value and adjusting it with swipes, keyboard and D-pad arrows) and styled with the Plenix tokens: the action color for the handle and the filled track, the Plenix gray for the rest, and a label with the current value above the track in DM Sans. Material’s default uses the theme’s primary and secondary container colors and shows the value only in a bubble while dragging; Plenix keeps Material’s sizes and structure and replaces the colors and type. android-forms|Switch.summary: A Plenix switch on Android is the Material 3 Switch in a full-width row, kept native in behavior (the whole row toggles, the thumb slides and grows on press, TalkBack reads it as a switch with its label and state, font scale) and styled with the Plenix tokens: the action color for on, the Plenix gray track for off, a white thumb with no icon, and the label in DM Sans at the body text role at the start of a 48 dp row. Material’s default draws an outlined off track with a small dark thumb in the theme colors; Plenix keeps Material’s sizes and structure and replaces the colors and type. A switch takes effect at once; a choice saved later with a button is a checkbox.

The question is the Plenix alert dialog (Material 3’s dialog with the Plenix look): the title names the action and the count (“Delete 2 categories?”), the body says the consequence and lists what goes, and the confirm button says the verb, in the danger colors when it destroys. android-patterns|Sign-in and account.summary: Plenix on Android signs people in, up and back in through the platform’s Credential Manager first (passkeys, saved passwords, Sign in with Google), and with a form when needed: OutlinedTextFields whose autofill types the platform understands (username, password, newPassword, smsOtpCode), a password field with a trailing Show toggle, one general error above the fields, and the primary button as wide as the form at the 48 dp target. The second step takes the code from the SMS Retriever or the user’s paste; a session about to end is an AlertDialog that keeps the work; each linked service is a list row with its status in words. On a compact window the form fills the screen under the top app bar; on medium and expanded windows it sits in a card a small dialog wide, as on the web.

ios-actions|Context menus.summary: A Plenix context menu on iOS is the system context menu (UIContextMenuInteraction), kept native in behavior: a touch and hold or a secondary click opens it, a lifted preview confirms the target, the background dims and VoiceOver reads the actions. Plenix decides what it holds: only the commands that apply to that item, at most three groups, the most used nearest the item, destructive items last and marked, and every command also reachable in the main interface. The system draws the menu and its glass; where Plenix draws a menu itself it uses the Plenix menu tokens shown in the Plenix rows, and the preview keeps the item’s own shape.

ios-actions|Edit menus.summary: A Plenix edit menu on iOS is the system edit menu (UIEditMenuInteraction), never a copy of it: it opens with the standard gestures on a text or content selection, lays out horizontally for touch and vertically for a pointer, moves aside when it would cover the selection, and works with VoiceOver and the keyboard. ios-actions|Undo and redo.summary: Plenix undo on iOS keeps the system’s undo (UndoManager, shake to undo, the three-finger gestures and Command-Z on a keyboard) and adds the Plenix undo toast for actions that remove or change many things at once: a delete, a move to the trash, an unpublish. The toast says what happened in DM Sans on the inverse surface, holds Undo while it shows, and leaves after the toast duration; the action is final only then. Every action that registers an undo names it, so the system’s Undo menu says Undo Delete.

ios-data-display|Charts.summary: The Plenix chart on iOS is a Swift Charts chart in the Plenix frame: a title and a one-sentence takeaway above it, marks in the data-viz colors by the series’ order, light grid lines, tick labels in DM Mono, and the same data as a list or table one tap away. Swift Charts keeps its own layout, scrolling, selection and accessibility (the audio graph and the per-mark VoiceOver labels); Plenix sets the look and the content rules that ChartFrame sets on the web. The charts of wave 9 follow it: lines, steps and areas are LineMark and AreaMark, a heat map RectangleMark, a waterfall BarMark with a start and an end; a word cloud, a network graph and a diagram are custom layouts or a Canvas with an accessibility element per item.

ios-data-display|Outline views.summary: Plenix on iOS shows a library’s folders the way the web’s file browser does: an outline of folders in the sidebar or the primary column, each row a folder symbol and its name in DM Sans, the open folder in the selected fill, and its contents in a list beside or after it, files with their names and facts in DM Mono. Apple’s default is the system’s hierarchical list with its disclosure indicators; Plenix keeps the outline’s structure, its disclosure, its keyboard and VoiceOver behavior, and changes the look: Plenix colors, DM Sans and DM Mono, the Plenix row height and the line between rows. Files move by dragging them onto a folder or with Move to in the row’s menu.

ios-feedback|Notifications.summary: A Plenix notification on iOS is a system notification (UserNotifications), drawn entirely by the system on the Lock Screen, in Notification Center and as a banner, with the app icon, SF Pro text and the system glass; no app can restyle it. ios-feedback|Progress indicators.summary: A Plenix progress indicator on iOS is the system ProgressView (UIProgressView and UIActivityIndicatorView), kept native in behavior: it reports its value to VoiceOver, animates with the system, and respects Reduce Motion. Plenix changes the look to match the Web ProgressBar and Spinner: an 8-point pill track in the Plenix neutral fill with a fill in the tone color (info by default, success, warning or danger), a DM Sans label that names the task, an optional muted value in tabular digits, and a spinner in the Plenix primary action color. uikit: /// The Plenix stepper in UIKit: a UIStepper drawn with Plenix background and divider images.
func plenixImage(_ color: Color, width: CGFloat = Plenix.Border.borderWidthThin, radius: CGFloat = Plenix.Radius.radiusControl) -> UIImage {
let size = CGSize(width: max(width, radius * 2 + Plenix.Border.borderWidthThin), height: 32)   // 32: Apple’s UIStepper height; the middle stretches
UIBezierPath(roundedRect: CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size), cornerRadius: radius).fill()

ios-navigation|Sidebars.summary: A Plenix sidebar on iOS is the system sidebar list (a List with the sidebar style in a NavigationSplitView, or a UICollectionView sidebar layout), kept native in behavior: it shows by default, hides with the usual gesture or command, folds disclosure groups, floats over rich content on iPad, and supports Dynamic Type, VoiceOver and the keyboard. ios-navigation|Tab bars.summary: A Plenix tab bar on iOS is the system TabView (UITabBarController), kept native in behavior: it floats over the content, minimizes on scroll, keeps the search tab at its trailing end, becomes a sidebar on iPad, and supports Dynamic Type, VoiceOver and the keyboard. Plenix keeps the system glass material and changes the look of the items: filled symbols at 20 points, DM Sans labels at the caption text role, the Plenix muted color for tabs that are not selected, the Plenix selected color for the current tab and the Plenix danger color for badges. It is the iOS form of the Web mobile navigation bar.

ios-overlays|Action sheets.summary: A Plenix action sheet on iOS keeps the system sheet’s structure and behavior: it rises from the bottom after the person starts an action, lists a few choices with destructive ones first and Cancel last, closes on a choice, a tap outside or Escape, and becomes a popover on iPad. The system confirmation dialog takes only a tint, so the full Plenix look draws the sheet as a bottom panel with the Plenix menu tokens: the overlay surface, the 8-point menu radius, rows 44 points tall with DM Sans at the body text role, hairline dividers and the danger content color for destructive choices. Apple’s default is a Liquid Glass panel of capsule buttons in SF Pro.

ios-overlays|Alerts.summary: A Plenix alert on iOS keeps the system alert’s structure and behavior: a modal card centered over a dimmed screen, a title, an optional message and text field, and one to three actions, with Cancel answering Escape and the cancel gestures, and VoiceOver kept inside the alert. Apple’s default is a Liquid Glass card with capsule buttons and SF Pro text.

ios-patterns|Drag and drop.summary: Drag and drop on iOS keeps the system’s own drag: a long press lifts the item with the system preview, items move within and between lists and apps, and VoiceOver offers the same moves as custom actions. Plenix styles what the app draws around it: the lifted row on the raised surface with the overlay shadow, the insertion line and the drop target’s dashed outline in the focus ring’s color, a refusing target in the danger color with words, and a Move menu (and Move up, Move down in an edited list) so every drag has a way without dragging. Apple’s default is the system preview over the app’s own unstyled targets; Plenix keeps the system gesture and preview and replaces the app’s look.

ios-patterns|Managing accounts.summary: Plenix on iOS signs people in, up and back in with the system’s own help: Sign in with Apple and passkeys first where the service offers them, the password fields that the system’s password manager and the one-time-code autofill understand (textContentType username, password, newPassword, oneTimeCode), and the session ending with an alert that keeps the work. Plenix styles what the app draws: the form on the grouped surface with the Plenix field border and fill, the primary button as wide as the form at the touch height, one general error above the fields, the links to the other flows as plain buttons, and every account’s connection as a row with its status in words. Apple’s default is a plain Form; Plenix keeps its structure and the system sheets and changes the look.

ios-specialized|File management.summary: Plenix on iOS shows files and folders the way the web does and leaves choosing, opening and saving to the system: the document picker and the document browser, Quick Look for previews, the share sheet for sending. A file is its type’s symbol (or a thumbnail from QuickLookThumbnailing), its name with the extension kept in view when a long name is cut, and its size and date in DM Mono; a folder is the folder symbol, its name in DM Sans and its count. In a list each file is a row with its facts and a trailing menu of Rename, Download and Delete; during a transfer the row shows a linear progress view and Cancel. Apple’s default is the system list row; Plenix keeps the row, its swipe actions and its context menu and changes the look.

swiftui: // Use the existing semantic tokens and a visible AI origin label; no AI color.
// Keep generated content in state while requests run.
// A source is a native Link; a disclosure opens source details without navigating.
// Cancel obsolete search tasks; only the latest request may replace the result.
uikit: // UIStackView composes the origin label, content, source links and explicit actions.
// Keep prior text during an async regenerate and retain it on errors.
// Use a real link control for each source; do not claim sources are verified.
appkit: // Compose an origin label and explicit actions from existing AppKit controls.
// NSPopover shows source details; a link navigates only after activation.
// Retain the current version until the caller supplies the regenerated result.
